channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United Kingdom: Burnham sentiment bounce – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a sharp improvement in sentiment towards Prime Minister Burnham and Labour.

item.title: S&P Global US PMIs expected to ease slightly in August, still showing solid growth
item.description: S&P Global will release the preliminary figures of August’s United States Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs), a report collecting top private sector executives' opinions about business conditions, to provide an early indication of momentum in the world’s largest economy.

item.title: United States: Yields risk renewed surge – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior US Strategist Philip Marey discusses United States (US) Treasuries, noting that the Treasury Department’s surprise move to boost buybacks of longer-term bonds has only briefly interrupted rising yields.

item.title: 1.3670: British Pound hits six-month highs as UK PMI beats expectations
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) rallied to fresh six-month highs against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, boosted by stronger-than-expected UK business activity data, while the US Dollar remains depressed following the US Treasury’s plan to boost bond buybacks.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $69.94 per troy ounce, up 2.67% from the $68.12 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains under pressure amid higher oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) ticks lower against the US Dollar (USD) in India's afternoon trading hours on Friday. The USD/INR edges up to near 95.72 as elevated oil prices and a sharp recovery in United States (US) Treasury yields have weighed on the Indian currency.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank keeps tightening option open – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke reports that the Riksbank left its policy rate at 1.75% and maintained a restrictive stance, still seeing a hike later this year as likely.

item.title: ECB’s Kazāks: Central bank is well placed to act if needed to get inflation to 2%
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Mārtiņš Kazāks said during the European trading session on Friday that the central bank won’t hesitate to act if needed to bring Eurozone inflationary pressures down to the 2% target.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness offsets intervention impact – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Michael Wan notes that US longer-end yields have returned close to pre-buyback levels, with the 10-year at 4.7% and 30-year at 5.24%, weighing on risk assets.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Oil supply tightness supports further upside above $90
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade flat near $86.00 during the European trading session on Friday, closer to its over three-week high of $87.38 posted the previous day.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer bias with pro-risk flows – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner, Francesco Pesole and Frantisek Taborsky argue that recent US Treasury buy-backs are primarily a signalling tool against high yields, pointing to a softer Dollar in a risk-friendly environment.

item.title: Gold rallies to its highest level since late May, eyes $4,600 on weak USD ahead of US PMIs
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) builds on the intraday breakout momentum above a technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) and climbs to its highest level since late May during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Euro steadies against British Pound as strong PMIs offer support on both sides
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8570 on Friday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen sticks to gains amid hawkish BoJ bets as USD stays weak on Fed expectations
item.description: The USD/JPY pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's recovery from the 158.00 mark, or a one-and-a-half-week low, and meets with fresh supply on Friday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Backstop doubts and high intervention bar – BNY
item.description: BNY’s David Tam stresses that while the Federal Reserve retains legal capacity to support corporate credit, the current Warsh Fed is unlikely to repeat Covid‑era interventions.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Inflation re-acceleration weighs on PLN – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose highlights growing challenges for Polish policymakers, citing stretched fiscal plans and accelerating underlying inflation.

item.title: United Kingdom flash Services PMI expands faster to 52.8 in August, beats 51.8 estimates
item.description: The United Kingdom (UK) S&P Global Composite Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) expanded surprisingly at a faster pace to 52.5 in August due to robust service sector activity. The Composite PMI was expected to arrive lower at 51.6 from 52.2 in July.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Range-bound with mild upside against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/JPY at 159.00 rebounded sharply from 158.00, but now looks set to trade between 158.50 and 159.35 intraday.

item.title: Euro holds near three-month highs as Eurozone Flash PMIs beat expectations
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is trading a few pips below 1.1700 against a depressed US Dollar (USD) on Friday, on track for a more than 1% weekly rally, and with the three-month high of 1.1710 at a short distance.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Extreme shorts face a high bar for further losses – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny sees a tension between aggressive Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) tightening expectations and increasingly stretched short positioning in the New Zealand Dollar (NZD).

item.title: Canadian Dollar stands firm near three-month high vs weak USD ahead of data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair remains under some selling pressure for the third consecutive day and trades near a three-month low, just above mid-1.3700s during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Eurozone flash Manufacturing PMI rises unexpectedly faster-than-estimates to 52.8 in August
item.description: Preliminary HCOB Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) in the Eurozone expands surprisingly at a faster pace to 52.8 in August from 51.9 in July. Manufacturing activity was anticipated to expand at a moderate pace to 51.8.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Funding role grows as volatility stays low – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING explains that USD/CHF’s sharp drop after the US Treasury buy-back announcement was mainly position adjustment after a hawkish Fed narrative had favoured longs.

item.title: US Dollar: Consolidation around 99.00 after buyback news – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chang Wei Liang notes that the Dollar has firmed slightly as US Treasury yields recover, with DXY consolidating near 99.00 after the US Treasury expanded long-end bond buybacks.

item.title: Dow Jones futures gain as traders weigh US debt buybacks against surging oil prices
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.13% to trade above 52,900 during European hours on Friday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures remain up by 0.18%, to trade near 7,680, and Nasdaq 100 futures advance by 0.38% to trade above 29,400.

item.title: Euro remains weaker against Canadian Dollar following German PMI data
item.description: EUR/CAD extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 1.6100 during the European hours on Friday. The currency cross depreciates as the Euro (EUR) holds losses following the release of HCOB Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data from Germany.

item.title: Japanese Yen: September BoJ risk builds – Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank argues that July inflation and strong Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data in Japan suggest price dynamics would not block a Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hike.

item.title: Germany’s flash Manufacturing PMI unexpectedly rises faster to 54.1 vs. 52.0 estimates
item.description: German flash HCOB Composite PMI rises moderately to 51.0 in August as the services sector activity contracts again. The Composite PMI was expected to remain steady at 51.3.

item.title: British Pound: Upward momentum targets 1.3700 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports GBP/USD at 1.3640 remains supported after breaking key resistance levels, with intraday gains likely capped between 1.3605 and 1.3670.

item.title: Euro: Gentle upside against US Dollar as greenback softens - ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner says EUR/USD remains well supported by broad Dollar softness. Expected mild eurozone growth in the August PMIs and elevated inflation expectations keep the case for another European Central Bank (ECB) hike alive.
